ai-addendum.name: AI Addendum
ai-addendum.description: Layers AI-specific terms onto an existing agreement: how the customer may use AI services, restrictions such as regulated decision-making without human oversight, model training, ownership of input and output, and disclaimers about the nature of AI.

fields.label: Training Data
fields.guide: What data, if any, the provider may use to train a model. Leaving this empty forbids training altogether.

fields.label: Training Purposes
fields.guide: What the provider may train a model for. Only meaningful if training data is identified.

fields.label: Training Restrictions
fields.guide: Limits on training beyond the stated purposes. Often empty.

fields.label: Improvement Restrictions
fields.guide: Limits on using input and output to improve the AI system short of training it. Often empty.

business-associate-agreement.name: Business Associate Agreement
business-associate-agreement.description: HIPAA business associate agreement between a covered entity and a service provider handling protected health information, covering obligations, permitted uses and disclosures, breach notification, and term and termination.

fields.label: Agreement
fields.guide: The underlying agreement this BAA attaches to, named so both sides know what it supplements.

fields.label: BAA Effective Date
fields.guide: The day this BAA starts.

fields.label: Breach Notification Period
fields.guide: How long the provider has to report an impermissible use or disclosure of PHI, such as 5 business days.

fields.label: Limitations
fields.guide: Any restrictions on the provider passing PHI to subcontractors. Often empty.

cloud-service-agreement.name: Cloud Service Agreement
cloud-service-agreement.description: Standard terms for a SaaS or cloud product subscription, covering access and use, support, customer content, fees and payment, term and termination, warranties, limitation of liability, and indemnification.

fields.label: Effective Date
fields.guide: The day the framework terms start.

fields.label: Order Date
fields.guide: The day this particular order starts, which may be later than the effective date.

fields.label: Subscription Period
fields.guide: How long each subscription runs before it renews, such as 12 months.

fields.label: Non-Renewal Notice Date
fields.guide: The last day either side can give notice to stop the subscription renewing.

fields.label: Technical Support
fields.guide: What support the provider commits to, and how the customer reaches it.

fields.label: Use Limitations
fields.guide: Caps on how much of the service the customer may use, such as seats, calls or storage.

fields.label: Payment Process
fields.guide: How the customer is billed and pays: invoicing, card on file, or something else.

fields.label: DPA
fields.guide: The data processing agreement between the parties, if they have one. Often empty.

fields.label: Governing Law
fields.guide: One US state, spelled out in full, whose law governs.

fields.label: Chosen Courts
fields.guide: Where disputes are heard, such as the state and federal courts in New Castle County, Delaware.

fields.label: General Cap Amount
fields.guide: The ceiling on each side's total liability for ordinary claims.

fields.label: Increased Claims
fields.guide: Which kinds of claim get a higher liability ceiling than the general one. Often empty.

fields.label: Increased Cap Amount
fields.guide: The higher ceiling that applies to increased claims. Meaningless unless increased claims are listed.

fields.label: Unlimited Claims
fields.guide: Which kinds of claim escape the liability caps entirely. Often empty.

fields.label: Additional Warranties
fields.guide: Promises either side makes beyond the standard ones. Often empty.

fields.label: Provider Covered Claims
fields.guide: The claims against the customer that the provider will defend and pay for.

fields.label: Customer Covered Claims
fields.guide: The claims against the provider that the customer will defend and pay for.

data-processing-agreement.name: Data Processing Agreement
data-processing-agreement.description: GDPR-oriented agreement between a controller and a processor, covering subprocessors, processing instructions, international transfers, security incidents, audits, data subject requests, and deletion.

fields.label: Agreement
fields.guide: The underlying agreement this DPA attaches to.

fields.label: Nature and Purpose of Processing
fields.guide: What the provider does with the personal data, and why.

fields.label: Categories of Personal Data
fields.guide: What kinds of personal data are processed, such as names, email addresses or usage logs.

fields.label: Categories of Data Subjects
fields.guide: Whose personal data it is: customers, employees, end users, and so on.

fields.label: Special Category Data
fields.guide: Any sensitive data under Article 9, such as health or biometric data. Often empty.

fields.label: Special Category Data Restrictions or Safeguards
fields.guide: Extra protections applied to special category data. Meaningless unless there is any.

fields.label: Duration of Processing
fields.guide: How long the provider keeps processing the data, usually tied to the underlying agreement.

fields.label: Frequency of Transfer
fields.guide: How often data moves across borders: continuously, or on a one-off basis.

fields.label: Approved Subprocessors
fields.guide: The subprocessors the customer has already approved, or where that list is published.

fields.label: Governing Member State
fields.guide: The EEA member state whose law governs the standard contractual clauses.

fields.label: Security Policy
fields.guide: The security standard the provider is audited against, or a link to it.

fields.label: Provider Security Contact
fields.guide: Where the customer sends security questions and audit requests.

design-partner-agreement.name: Design Partner Agreement
design-partner-agreement.description: Early-stage collaboration in which a design partner uses a pre-release product and gives feedback, covering scope of participation, fees, term and termination, warranty disclaimers, confidentiality, and ownership of feedback.

fields.label: Effective Date
fields.guide: The day the agreement starts.

fields.label: Term
fields.guide: How long the partner keeps early access, such as 6 months.

fields.label: Program
fields.guide: What taking part actually involves: what the partner tries, and how they report back.

fields.label: Fees
fields.guide: What the partner pays, if anything. Design partnerships are often free, and an empty answer is a good one.

fields.label: Governing Law
fields.guide: One US state, spelled out in full, whose law governs.

fields.label: Chosen Courts
fields.guide: Where disputes are heard, such as the state and federal courts in New Castle County, Delaware.

partnership-agreement.name: Partnership Agreement
partnership-agreement.description: Commercial partnership such as a reseller or referral arrangement, covering cooperation, payment and taxes, trademark licence, privacy, escalation, term and termination, warranties, and limitation of liability.

fields.label: Effective Date
fields.guide: The day the partnership starts.

fields.label: End Date
fields.guide: The day it ends, unless someone terminates it earlier.

fields.label: Obligations
fields.guide: What each side actually commits to do. This is the heart of the deal.

fields.label: Territory
fields.guide: Where the partner may use the other side's brand and sell, such as the United States or worldwide.

fields.label: Brand Guidelines
fields.guide: Rules for using the other side's name and logo, or a link to them. Often empty.

fields.label: Payment Process
fields.guide: How one side bills the other for fees.

fields.label: Payment Schedule
fields.guide: When those payments fall due, such as net 30 from invoice.

fields.label: DPA
fields.guide: The data processing agreement between the parties, if they have one. Often empty.

fields.label: Governing Law
fields.guide: One US state, spelled out in full, whose law governs.

fields.label: Chosen Courts
fields.guide: Where disputes are heard, such as the state and federal courts in New Castle County, Delaware.

fields.label: General Cap Amount
fields.guide: The ceiling on each side's total liability for ordinary claims.

fields.label: Increased Claims
fields.guide: Which kinds of claim get a higher liability ceiling than the general one. Often empty.

fields.label: Increased Cap Amount
fields.guide: The higher ceiling that applies to increased claims. Meaningless unless increased claims are listed.

fields.label: Unlimited Claims
fields.guide: Which kinds of claim escape the liability caps entirely. Often empty.

fields.label: Additional Warranties
fields.guide: Promises either side makes beyond the standard ones. Often empty.

fields.label: Company Covered Claim
fields.guide: The claims against the partner that the company will defend and pay for.

fields.label: Partner Covered Claims
fields.guide: The claims against the company that the partner will defend and pay for.

pilot-agreement.name: Pilot Agreement
pilot-agreement.description: Short paid or free trial of a product, covering pilot access and use, user accounts, customer content, feedback, confidentiality, term and termination, and limitation of liability.

fields.label: Effective Date
fields.guide: The day the pilot starts.

fields.label: Pilot Period
fields.guide: How long the customer may use the product for evaluation, such as 60 days.

fields.label: Governing Law
fields.guide: One US state, spelled out in full, whose law governs.

fields.label: Chosen Courts
fields.guide: Where disputes are heard, such as the state and federal courts in New Castle County, Delaware.

fields.label: General Cap Amount
fields.guide: The ceiling on each side's total liability.

professional-services-agreement.name: Professional Services Agreement
professional-services-agreement.description: Framework for professional services delivered under statements of work, covering deliverables and acceptance, subcontractors, intellectual property assignment, payment, insurance, warranties, and limitation of liability.

fields.label: Effective Date
fields.guide: The day the framework agreement starts.

fields.label: SOW Term
fields.guide: How long a statement of work runs once signed.

fields.label: Deliverables
fields.guide: What the provider is actually handing over, as distinct from the work itself.

fields.label: Rejection Period
fields.guide: How long the customer has to reject a deliverable before it counts as accepted.

fields.label: Resubmission Period
fields.guide: How long the provider then has to fix and resubmit it.

fields.label: Time of Assignment
fields.guide: When ownership of the deliverables passes to the customer: on payment, on acceptance, or on creation.

fields.label: Fees
fields.guide: What the customer pays, and on what basis: fixed price, time and materials, or a rate card.

fields.label: Payment Period
fields.guide: How long the customer has to pay an invoice, such as net 30.

fields.label: Customer Obligations
fields.guide: What the customer must do for the work to proceed: access, data, people, decisions. Often empty.

fields.label: Customer Policies
fields.guide: Customer rules the provider must follow on site or on their systems. Often empty.

fields.label: Security Policy
fields.guide: The security standard the provider must meet, or a link to it. Often empty.

fields.label: Insurance Minimums
fields.guide: The cover each side must carry, if any. Often empty.

fields.label: DPA
fields.guide: The data processing agreement between the parties, if they have one. Often empty.

fields.label: Governing Law
fields.guide: One US state, spelled out in full, whose law governs.

fields.label: Chosen Courts
fields.guide: Where disputes are heard, such as the state and federal courts in New Castle County, Delaware.

fields.label: General Cap Amount
fields.guide: The ceiling on each side's total liability for ordinary claims.

fields.label: Increased Claims
fields.guide: Which kinds of claim get a higher liability ceiling than the general one. Often empty.

fields.label: Increased Cap Amount
fields.guide: The higher ceiling that applies to increased claims. Meaningless unless increased claims are listed.

fields.label: Unlimited Claims
fields.guide: Which kinds of claim escape the liability caps entirely. Often empty.

fields.label: Additional Warranties
fields.guide: Promises either side makes beyond the standard ones. Often empty.

fields.label: Provider Covered Claims
fields.guide: The claims against the customer that the provider will defend and pay for.

fields.label: Customer Covered Claims
fields.guide: The claims against the provider that the customer will defend and pay for.

service-level-agreement.name: Service Level Agreement
service-level-agreement.description: Defines the uptime commitment and how availability and downtime are measured, support response time targets, and the service credits available when a commitment is missed.

fields.label: Target Uptime
fields.guide: The availability the provider commits to each month, such as 99.9 percent.

fields.label: Uptime Credit
fields.guide: What the customer gets back when uptime falls short, usually a percentage of the monthly fee.

fields.label: Scheduled Downtime
fields.guide: Planned maintenance windows that do not count against uptime. Often empty.

fields.label: Target Response Time
fields.guide: How quickly the provider acknowledges a support request, such as 4 business hours.

fields.label: Response Time Credit
fields.guide: What the customer gets back when a response target is missed.

fields.label: Support Channel
fields.guide: Where the customer sends support requests: an email address, a portal, or a phone number.

fields.label: Subscription Period
fields.guide: The billing period uptime is measured against, taken from the underlying subscription.

software-license-agreement.name: Software License Agreement
software-license-agreement.description: Licence for software installed and run by the customer, covering the licence grant and limits, restrictions, support, fees, warranties, indemnification, and limitation of liability.

fields.label: Effective Date
fields.guide: The day the framework terms start.

fields.label: Order Date
fields.guide: The day this particular order starts, which may be later than the effective date.

fields.label: Subscription Period
fields.guide: How long the licence runs before it renews, such as 12 months.

fields.label: Non-Renewal Notice Date
fields.guide: The last day either side can give notice to stop the licence renewing.

fields.label: Permitted Uses
fields.guide: What the customer is allowed to do with the software, and on whose systems.

fields.label: License Limits
fields.guide: Caps on the licence: seats, installations, cores, environments.

fields.label: Warranty Period
fields.guide: How long the provider warrants the software matches its specifications.

fields.label: Deletion Procedure
fields.guide: How the customer removes the software when the licence ends.

fields.label: Payment Process
fields.guide: How the customer is billed and pays: invoicing, card on file, or something else.

fields.label: Governing Law
fields.guide: One US state, spelled out in full, whose law governs.

fields.label: Chosen Courts
fields.guide: Where disputes are heard, such as the state and federal courts in New Castle County, Delaware.

fields.label: Increased Cap Amount

fields.label: Unlimited Claims
fields.guide: Which kinds of claim escape the liability caps entirely. Often empty.

fields.label: Additional Warranties
fields.guide: Promises either side makes beyond the standard ones. Often empty.
